Hi Tanya —

Following up on our invoice INV-2027-1184 for the June usage period (total due: $43,720.00). We wanted to make the payment path as smooth as possible for your AP team:

- We can pull ACH on Thursday, 24 Jun, if you approve an ACH-pull authorization (attached).
- Alternatively we can accept a one-time wire on or before 24 Jun; wire instructions are on the invoice PDF attached.

To reduce manual steps, we can also provision your AP contact with our billing portal where remittance info, invoices and W-9s are available. Granting portal access usually trims reconciliation time. If you prefer, I can loop in our onboarding engineer for a 15-min screen share.

Can you confirm:
1) AP contact who will approve the ACH pull (name + email)
2) Whether Granite AI requires a PO number on the payment (we currently have PO: N/A)
3) If we should go ahead and schedule the ACH pull for 24 Jun if we get signed authorization by EOD Tuesday (22 Jun).

I've attached the invoice, our W-9 and the ACH pull authorization form for your review.

Thanks —
Rachel
Rachel Kim

rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for the note. A few items from our side:

1) AP approver is me (Tanya Morgan) — please send any authorization forms to ap@graniteai.com.
2) Granite AI does not require a PO for vendor invoices under $50k, so no PO is needed for this invoice.
3) We prefer to do ACH but need a shortened remittance reference to match our ERP. Could you confirm the remittance string you will push so we can map it to our invoice batch?

Also, our tax team needs the Redwood entity name used on the W-9 to match our vendor record — the PDF you attached lists "Redwood Inference, Inc.", but our vendor master shows "Redwood Labs, Inc." (we received both names from prior vendor records). Can you confirm the legal entity we should capture to avoid tax withholding?

If the ACH pull is scheduled, we require the signed authorization by 22 Jun EOD. We can accept a scanned signature on the PDF.

Tanya

- Legal entity: The correct legal payee is "Redwood Inference, Inc." — the W-9 attached is the one for the entity that appears on your invoice (we're standardizing names across our finance systems this quarter). Apologies for the confusion.

Next steps if that's all good:

2) I'll attach an updated W-9 with the employer identification number masked for email, and resend the ACH auth with a signature block if you'd like to sign digitally.
